Komoro Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ungvári utca 1, Hungary

Not demolished. Komoró's Jewish population peaked at 88 people in 1870, then steadily declined to just 8 by 1941, among a total population of 1,082. This cemetery, established as early as 1870, per that year's cadastral map, sits today within the local municipal cemetery, used as an auxiliary area for bike storage and a compost heap. In mid-April 1944, Komoró's Jews were deported via the Kisvárda Ghetto to Auschwitz; only a single person returned to the village afterward, in 1949, and remained the settlement's only Jew.
